column1: SAMIR: keep REINDEX usable when the navigation cache is cold
column4: Root: os/samir/cmd/mutate.c:980 clears navigation after PACK. REINDEX at :1110 calls os/samir/fs/ndx.c:2671, which closes the index before ndx_build invokes its key provider (:1378). That provider calls wa_nav_goto (mutate.c:1093); os/samir/cmd/nav.c:344 materializes the master order through the now-closed index when the cache is cold. ndx_rebuild:2679 returns without reopening on provider failure, leaving fd=-1. Key collection must use physical navigation independent of the index being rebuilt; failure must leave a usable or explicitly detached handle. Ground truth: ../dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/data-definition-and-manipulation.md sec.10/sec.15 require PACK/REINDEX to maintain open indexes. The audit one-index control warms navigation before REINDEX; index count is not the isolated trigger. Acceptance oracle: Extend harness/diff/dbf_diff/test_ndx_pack.c and test_samir_dml.c with cold/warm caches, 1/2/7 indexes, each master order, and PACK with/without deletions. Drive PACK; REINDEX; GO TOP; LIST before any intervening read, then SEEK on every order. Check independent NDX traversal and DBF records; inject provider failure and replay pack-two.json on copied images. A mutant restoring index-aware key collection after closing the master must fail the cold-cache case. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/pack-two.json, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/pack-two-serial.log, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/pack-index.json, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/pack-index-serial.log, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/pack-two-files/BYNAME.NDX, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/pack-two-files/BYBAL.NDX, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/shots/pack-two-after.png.

column1: SAMIR: remove failed new INDEX, SORT and COPY FILE outputs so retry works
column4: Root: os/samir/fs/ndx.c:1472 creates/truncates output, but :1500 and later failed-write exits only close it. os/samir/cmd/mutate.c:1202-1209 creates SORT output and closes on failure without remove; :1294 and :1309-1323 do the same for COPY FILE. d_destination at :1084-1085 then rejects the abandoned name under SAFETY. Use one owned-output failure/commit policy across these paths; never delete a pre-existing destination as failed-new-file cleanup. Ground truth: ../dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/data-definition-and-manipulation.md sec.15 describes deleting an incomplete interrupted index; DBF/NDX format invariants require complete structures. Removal or safe staging of failed new SORT/COPY outputs is the audit recovery requirement, not a claim of historical transaction guarantees. Acceptance oracle: Extend test_samir_dml.c, test_ndx_build.c and PAL fault injection across create, each short/failed write, and close. Verify source hashes, SAFETY and existing targets survive. At zero free clusters, run full-recovery, free FILLER.BIN and retry all three names without manual ERASE; extract valid outputs with mtools and independently parse DBF/NDX. A mutant omitting cleanup must leave a zero-byte name and fail the retry assertion. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/full-recovery-serial.log, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/full-recovery-bytes.json, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/full-recovery-files/FULLIDX.NDX, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/full-recovery-files/SORTED.DBF, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/full-recovery-files/COPIED.DBF, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/shots/full-recovery-failure.png.

column1: SAMIR: refresh the live memo reader after a successful replacement
column4: Root: os/samir/fs/dbf.c:1763-1770 appends through a separate writable DBT handle and publishes the new pointer. The work area retains its reader (os/samir/cmd/workarea.c:487/:903). os/samir/fs/dbt.c:521-531 already refreshes next_free, contrary to the audit guess; Milton handles still retain independent file-size snapshots (os/milton/fileio_fat.c:39-43; os/milton/int21.c:3374). Reading the appended block through the old handle returns short, and workarea.c:905 converts that failure to empty text. Refresh/reopen the reader on successful write; do not require USE or hide real read errors as empty memos. Ground truth: ../dbase3-decomp/specs/file-formats/dbt.md sec.4/sec.8 and commands/data-definition-and-manipulation.md REPLACE; PRD 6.6 requires correct DBF/DBT round trips. This is a distinct same-session read-after-write defect; persisted text is correct. Acceptance oracle: Add a PAL with Milton-style per-open size snapshots to test_dbt_read.c/test_samir_core.c; a POSIX reader alone misses the defect. Repeat two replacements, direct reads, GO away/back and reopen; check lengths and DBF pointer/DBT bytes. Replay memo.json on desktop and DOS. A mutant retaining the old reader after append must return empty in the oracle and fail. Inject genuine short-read failures separately. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/memo.json, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/memo-serial.log, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/memo-files/EDGE.DBF, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/memo-files/EDGE.DBT, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/shots/memo-write.png.

column1: SAMIR: infer INDEX key geometry independently of the current record and enforce its limit
column4: Root: os/samir/cmd/mutate.c:1124-1130 evaluates the incoming current record to determine key type/width. os/samir/cmd/workarea.c:866 returns empty typed character values at EOF/empty, so ndx_build rejects zero key length (os/samir/fs/ndx.c:1336). The command also lacks a 100-byte key check; ndx_build validates page geometry only (:1339-1345), permitting the archived 101-byte key. Derive stable expression geometry including zero-record tables and report catalog 23 for oversize character keys. Ground truth: ../dbase3-decomp/specs/file-formats/ndx.md empty-root layout, commands/data-definition-and-manipulation.md sec.15, and spec/samir/dbase_msg_codes.tsv:31 (100 char maximum). Expression-source length is a different limit. The corpus marks precise boundary semantics oracle-resolves; mint III+ 100/101 cases before locking them. Acceptance oracle: Extend test_samir_dml.c/test_ndx_build.c for empty C(12), EOF/BOF/current-record permutations, expressions and 100/101/254-byte values. An empty index must reopen, SEEK miss and accept an append. Compare nonempty traversal with real III+ and independent decoded bytes; keep blank-date L016 on initech-ylqs. Replay index-fresh.json/index-boundary.json. Mutants using the current zero-width value or removing the cap must fail distinct cases. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/index-fresh-serial.log, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/fixtures/EMPTY.DBF, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/index-boundary-serial.log, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/index-boundary-files/KEY100.NDX, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/index-boundary-files/KEY101.NDX, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/shots/index-fresh-empty.png, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/shots/index-boundary-at-eof.png.

column1: SAMIR: accept complete 254-byte console commands with STATUS both off and on
column4: Root: os/samir/pal/pal_milton.c:650-654 selects application line input only with an active status screen; otherwise it frames AH=3Fh cooked console input. os/milton/int21.c:3227/:3252 intentionally cap that DOS editor at 128 bytes. Fix SAMIR console-input selection/framing, retaining the DOS handle contract and redirected streams. Consume an overlong application line without executing its truncated prefix. Ground truth: pubs/manuals/initechbase-volume-one/ua-keys.tex:20-22 and u2-commands.tex:16 promise 254 characters; ../dbase3-decomp/specs/runtime/interpreter-and-execution-model.md sec.2.1 independently defines the limit. The DOS staging buffer is not itself defective. Acceptance oracle: Extend test_samir_input.c/test_samir_repl.c and locked emulator traces for 127/128/129/253/254/255 characters, STATUS ON/OFF, both launches and redirected CRLF input. The 254-byte LEN case must return 245; 255 must raise 18 and leave the next command intact. Assert no truncated mutation executes. A mutant routing STATUS OFF back through 128-byte cooked input must fail. column1: SAMIR: run programs within the advertised byte limit regardless of short-line count
column4: Root: os/samir/cmd/flow.c:54 fixes FLOW_MAX_LINES at 512. samir_do at :1847-1867 uses fixed line/kind arrays and maps split_lines overflow to error 43; 7018-byte SHORT1K.PRG never executes although the loader permits 8191 bytes (os/samir/samir_main.c:459). Replace the hidden line-count bottleneck with bounded storage for the supported byte envelope. Simply growing automatic arrays aggravates the fixed-stack recursion defect on initech-39e5. Ground truth: pubs/manuals/initechbase-volume-one/u5-entries-a.tex:331-333 advertises 8191 characters without a 512-line restriction; the fixture is 7018 CRLF bytes. PRD 6.6 requires working program execution. This undocumented lower implementation limit is not deliberate canon. Acceptance oracle: Extend test_interp_flow.c/test_samir_repl.c for 511/512/513/1000 lines and the smallest-line worst case within 8191 bytes. SHORT1K must print 1000; over-byte-limit rejection must be clean. Include constrained PAL memory/guest stack bounds, a copied-image programedges trace and a subsequent command. A mutant restoring the 512-line cap must fail. Coordinate storage ownership with the recursion lane. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/fixtures/SHORT1K.PRG, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/programedges-serial.log, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/evidence/programs-real-serial.log, docs/audits/2026-10-23-samir/shots/programedges-1000.png.

column4: Root: os/samir/pal/pal_milton.c:581-596 emits ANSI cursor/attribute controls for the status screen. The FLAIR launch at os/milton/kmain.c:2946-2963 clears the raw console and executes SAMIR, bypassing DOS-path ANSI binding at :8082-8095. os/milton/int21.c:764 requires the binding/gate; raw os/milton/console.c:237-270 lacks BEL handling and paints byte 7. Bind terminal capabilities on desktop text launch and handle BEL without visible glyphs; preserve byte-transparent file output. Ground truth: pubs/manuals/initechbase-quick-reference/qr-set.tex:16 documents the status bar; ../dbase3-decomp/specs/full-screen/assist-ui-and-editors.md sec.10 describes it. BEL must not advance/paint text, per the audit terminal requirement. Intentional raw ANSI behavior without ANSI.SYS does not authorize an app to use unavailable controls. Acceptance oracle: Extend test_samir_status.c/test_samir_screen_emu.c and console/ANSI tests. Drive status ON/OFF, query, scroll and return on DOS/desktop; inspect guest pixels for bar/cursor and rejected-key BEL for no extra glyph/cursor movement. Verify redirected bytes and desktop restoration; record a record-flair clip. Mutants omitting desktop binding and rendering BEL as printable must each fail. Disk loading exists solely in os/samir/samir_main.c:550 and the outer REPL call at :675; no program-side fallback uses it. Ground truth: ../dbase3-decomp/specs/commands/programming-and-io.md:71-85 defines DO of a procedure or PRG. Same-name precedence is oracle-resolves; mint it. column4: Root: os/samir/cmd/flow.c:660 tokenizes @ but :872-897 gives it no form classification; os/samir/samir_main.c:593-615 registers no forms module and flow.c:1208 reports unknown verb. Terminal PAL slots exist (os/samir/include/samir/pal.h:148), but no GET list/READ consumer does. column4: Root: os/samir/samir_main.c:593-615 registers no program editor; query/mutate/set/proc/report hooks do not accept MODIFY, so os/samir/cmd/flow.c:1208 refuses it. The disk PRG loader at samir_main.c:472 supports execution only. First pickup: load FLOW.PRG, edit text, save/cancel and return to the session; retain broader editor commands on this feature. Mint III+ first-record/maintenance rules and independently traverse NDX while DBF row counts remain unchanged. Replay the ui-gaps unique case in an emulator. column4: Root: os/samir/cmd/query.c:451-490 handles scope/FOR/WHILE/OFF, so TO PRINT becomes expression text. os/samir/cmd/set.c:732-739 lacks MARGIN/PRINT/DEVICE branches. os/samir/cmd/workarea.c:1499-1506 routes to mirror/console only; PAL has no printer sink. Printer-position functions remain separately owned by initech-mgzg. Mint independent III+ output, add an emulator captured-printer leg and a no-printer leg reaching 126. Verify SCREEN/PRINT OFF controls. column1: SAMIR: preserve typed precondition and malformed-index errors at command boundaries
column4: Root: os/samir/cmd/set.c:415-417 maps all ndx_open_rw failures to missing-file ordinal 1. os/samir/cmd/mutate.c:609/:767/:917 returns syntax with ec=0 for absent tables, so the correct catalog mapper emits 10. Preserve typed causes at these hook boundaries: missing stays 1, malformed NDX gets its measured damaged-index code, and no database gets 52. This differs from old u78k internal-status/catalog collisions. Ground truth: spec/samir/dbase_msg_codes.tsv contains 1/52/114; ../dbase3-decomp/specs/file-formats/ndx.md defines header validation and commands/data-definition-and-manipulation.md gives table preconditions. Mint the precise III+ corrupt-index response; a present malformed file is definitely not nonexistent. Acceptance oracle: Extend test_interp_set.c/test_samir_repl.c for missing/truncated/bad-geometry NDX versus valid files, and DELETE/RECALL/PACK/REPLACE without a table versus genuine syntax errors. Replay errors.json/artifact-controls.json; assert no disk/work-area mutation. Mutants mapping malformed to 1 and no-table to 10 must each fail the error-class matrix.
